terra.problem: The joke mentions snacks, but cookies are the only food permitted in jokes.
The comparison doesn't make sense: a drawer with no room for anything new is not an empty stretch.
The joke makes Israel's sacred firstfruits image and the disaster that befell those who devoured her into a joke about taking from a tray.
The nicer-chair punchline makes light of the disaster in the verse.
The imagined quiet room adds a setting the passage does not give.
It turns what the verse says about Israel's fathers into a universal claim that everyone becomes like whatever they follow.
The explanation adds a reason the text does not give: that the idols had no power to give, so no power came back to their followers.
The text says they did not ask; it does not say they never thought to ask.
The text says they did not ask about the LORD, not that they did not think to ask about Him.
The junk-drawer joke makes light of the people's defilement of the land, and Papa's reference to being put in a drawer lacks the backstory needed to understand it.
Papa says he stayed loyal to the drawer, but he was stuck there and wanted to be put back to work.
The claim that this name appears elsewhere in Scripture needs a reference.
The loud-kitchen joke blends a kitchen into the passage's image and makes light of a scene of devastation.
The smoke-alarm comparison introduces blaming someone else, which is not the action in the verse. It also makes a joke out of Israel bringing devastation on himself.
Calling it a not-so-good drink adds a claim about the Nile's water that the passage does not make.
The explanation is generic and repeats that the river is the Nile without adding meaningful context or Papa's personality.
Beyond quoting the verse, the explanation only repeats that the statement is true. It lacks Papa's personality or an explanation of the verse.
